subject: RFI: Support ops, SLA windows & incident notification playbook
messages:
From: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@firsttrust.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@firsttrust.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Support operations / TAM coverage / incident notification

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this RFI. As part of our vendor evaluation we need a detailed response to Section 4: Support & Customer Success. Specifically: TAM coverage (hours, regions), escalation paths (contacts & SLA targets by severity), on-call rotation for TAM vs. Platform on-call, incident communication cadence and templates, and evidence of audit logging for customer incidents.

Can you confirm you can provide answers plus a short attachment with a matrix we can drop into our RFP? Our procurement deadline is EOD 16-Feb.

Best,
Sanjay
Sanjay Iyer
Head of Vendor Risk — FirstTrust Financial
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@firsttrust.com>
Cc: procurement@firsttrust.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Support operations / TAM coverage / incident notification

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear ask. We'll provide a concise RFP attachment and the escalation matrix. Initial notes below and attached: FT_RFP_Section4_Support_Qs.pdf (answers) and Redwood_TAM_Escalation_Matrix_v1.xlsx (contact matrix).

Quick summary:
- TAM coverage: 9am–6pm local business hours (Mon–Fri) by default; optional 24x7 coverage available for Dedicated/Private customers under our Support+ SLA addon.
- On-call split: Platform on-call (SRE) handles system incidents affecting multiple customers; Customer TAM handles customer communications, business context, and runbooks (TAM hands off to SRE for remediation where required).
- Escalation path: Tier 1 (TAM) -> Tier 2 (SRE engineer) -> Tier 3 (Eng on-call + Exec escalation). Severity definitions and response/restore targets in attached matrix.
- Notification: We provide an incident bridge within 15 minutes for Sev1s, periodic updates every 30–60 minutes until mitigation, post-incident summary within 48 hours.

I'll loop Priyom for the runbook and Karthik for any SLA/contract language you might need.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@firsttrust.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Support operations / TAM coverage / incident notification

Hi Sanjay —

Adding operational detail on runbooks / escalation SLAs and evidence you requested. Key items:

1) Severity mapping (short):
- Sev1 (Critical production outage): Response (bridge up) in <=15m, Engineering triage in <=30m, Target mitigations: partial mitigation <=2h, full restore RTO depends on root cause but SLA-backed credits only for Dedicated SLA customers.
- Sev2 (Partial outage / degraded): Response <=30m, mitigation in <=8h.
- Sev3 (Minor impact / API errors affecting small subset): Response <=4h, fix timeline best-effort.

2) Communication cadence:
- Bridge established at t=0 for Sev1; 30min updates until stable, then hourly until postmortem.
- For Sev2: 1–2 updates in first 8h, then daily until resolved.

3) Evidence and artifacts we can share: audit log extracts showing request/response traces (redacted), incident timelines (ops timeline), and anonymized runbook executions. We can generate a short export for your Security team.

Attached: a templated incident notification email and the escalation matrix. If you need SOC artifacts (SOC2 Type II report), we'll route that via your security contact / NDA.

Best,
Priyom Das
TAM Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@firsttrust.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@firsttrust.com, Oliver.Green <oliver.green@firsttrust.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Support operations / TAM coverage / incident notification

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. A couple clarifying items from our security review:
1) For shared audit logs, can you confirm retention window and redaction options? We generally need 12 months of event-level logs and the ability to produce a scoped extract for audits.
2) For Sev1 SLAs, where credits are only for Dedicated customers, can you provide sample SLA clause language and a fallback for Hosted customers (RPO/RTO expectations + escalation cadence)?

Also, please include the incident notification template and a sample postmortem format we can attach to the RFP.

Oliver (cc) is our infrastructure PM and will validate the runbook details.

Regards,
Sanjay
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@firsttrust.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@firsttrust.com
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Support operations / TAM coverage / incident notification

Hi Sanjay —

Quick answers to your two asks:

1) Audit logs: Standard retention for Hosted customers is 180 days; for Dedicated/Private we offer 12 months retention as part of the enterprise bundle. We can provide scoped exports (JSON/CSV) and apply redaction rules (PII removal) before delivery. If FirstTrust needs >12 months, we can add an extended-retention addendum.

2) SLA language: excerpt below (sample):
"For Dedicated Customers, Redwood guarantees 99.95% uptime per calendar month for the inference endpoint. For Hosted customers, Redwood offers commercially reasonable effort and a published operational status page; severity response timelines are as described in the RFI attachment. Formal SLA credits apply only to Dedicated contracts or with an explicit SLA addendum."

I'll attach a short SLA excerpt and a templated post-incident report to the Drive link. Vanessa — attaching redwood_mutual_action_plan_20270216.xlsx as discussed.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Product & GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
